evidence_text: The Computer History Museum records that Apple II debuted on April 16, 1977 at the first West Coast Computer Faire and was a hit.
decision: Introduce a fully assembled personal computer to a new general audience.
actual_change: Apple debuted the Apple II at the first West Coast Computer Faire.
before_state: Apple was a newly founded personal-computer company.
after_state: Apple had introduced its first mass-market product.
trigger: Demand for accessible personal computing beyond hobbyists.
outcome: The Apple II became Apple’s first mass-market computer.

evidence_text: Microsoft's official history records the April 7, 1975 headline: Altair BASIC is ready and working.
decision: Ship working BASIC software for the Altair microcomputer.
actual_change: Microsoft released working Altair BASIC.
before_state: A new software venture pursuing microcomputer users.
after_state: A working product was available for early microcomputer users.
trigger: Emergence of the Altair microcomputer.
outcome: Altair BASIC established Microsoft's first product launch.

evidence_text: Microsoft records that IBM introduced its PC with Microsoft's 16-bit operating system, MS-DOS 1.0, on August 12, 1981.
decision: Distribute an operating system through the IBM PC platform.
actual_change: IBM introduced its PC with Microsoft MS-DOS 1.0.
before_state: Microsoft sold microcomputer software products.
after_state: Microsoft entered the operating-system business through the IBM PC platform.
trigger: IBM personal-computer launch.
outcome: MS-DOS established a major operating-system distribution channel.

evidence_text: Microsoft announced retail shipment of Microsoft Windows on November 20, 1985.
decision: Launch Microsoft Windows as a graphical operating environment.
actual_change: Microsoft shipped Windows to retail dealers and distributors.
before_state: Microsoft's operating-system offering centered on MS-DOS.
after_state: Microsoft added a graphical operating environment to its product line.
trigger: Need for easier personal-computer interaction.
outcome: Windows began its commercial product lifecycle.

source_title: Here’s How a Four-Page Contract Started The Walt Disney Company
evidence_text: The Walt Disney Company states it officially began on October 16, 1923 when Walt Disney signed a contract to produce and distribute the Alice Comedies.
decision: Secure a distribution contract for the Alice Comedies.
actual_change: Walt Disney signed the contract to produce and distribute the Alice Comedies.
before_state: Walt Disney had moved to Hollywood after earlier studios failed.
after_state: The new studio had a distributor and a first production commitment.
trigger: A distributor needed new animated content.
outcome: The contract established the studio that became The Walt Disney Company.

evidence_text: Ford records that the first car built by Ford Motor Company was sold on July 15, 1903.

date_conflicts.evidence_text: Ford's biography dates the first car sale to July 15, 1903.
The Henry Ford chronology dates the company's first Model A sale to July 23, 1903.

decision: Sell the first car built by the company.
actual_change: Ford Motor Company sold its first car.
before_state: Ford Motor Company had just been created.
after_state: Ford had completed its first vehicle sale.
trigger: Initial automobile production.
outcome: The company converted its first manufactured car into a customer sale.

source_title: A Step Into The Future: GE Turns 130
evidence_text: GE records that Edison Electric Company merged with Thomson & Houston to form General Electric on April 15, 1892.
decision: Combine Edison Electric and Thomson & Houston into General Electric.
actual_change: Edison Electric Company merged with Thomson & Houston to form General Electric.
before_state: Two separate electrical companies.
after_state: A combined General Electric Company.
trigger: Strategic merger of electrical businesses.
outcome: General Electric was formed.

evidence_text: Walmart records that Sam Walton opened the first Walmart store in Rogers, Arkansas on July 2, 1962.
decision: Open the first Walmart discount store.
actual_change: Sam Walton opened the first Walmart store in Rogers, Arkansas.
before_state: Sam Walton’s prior retail operations.
after_state: A new Walmart discount-store format was operating.
trigger: Low-price retail strategy.
outcome: Walmart began operating its first store.

evidence_text: ExxonMobil records that Exxon and Mobil joined to form Exxon Mobil Corporation on November 30, 1999.
decision: Combine Exxon and Mobil into Exxon Mobil Corporation.
actual_change: Exxon and Mobil joined to form Exxon Mobil Corporation.
before_state: Exxon and Mobil operated as separate large energy companies.
after_state: A combined Exxon Mobil Corporation operated as an integrated energy company.
trigger: Need to strengthen global competitiveness in a more competitive energy industry.
outcome: Exxon Mobil Corporation was formed.

source_title: First Online DVD Rental Store Opens
evidence_text: Netflix's April 14, 1998 release announces the store opening that day. It describes more than 900 DVD titles, seven-day rentals, same-day shipping, prepaid return mailers and per-title pricing. These are launch terms, not measured retention or customer-validation results.
decision: Launch one complete rental workflow: choose a DVD online, pay per title, receive it by post and return it in a prepaid mailer.
actual_change: On April 14, 1998, Netflix opened an online store with over 900 DVD titles, seven-day rentals and postal fulfillment. The first two rental titles cost $4 each, with shipping charged separately.
before_state: Netflix was a company founded in 1997 preparing its online rental service.
after_state: United States DVD owners could rent or buy online; Netflix advertised same-day dispatch and two-to-three-day delivery.
trigger: Management identified inconvenient access to a broad DVD rental selection as the customer problem.
outcome: The rental workflow was publicly available. This release does not establish paid-customer counts, repeat usage, profitability or product-market fit.

source_title: Tesla Motors Begins Regular Production of 2008 Tesla Roadster
evidence_text: Tesla states regular production of the 2008 Tesla Roadster commenced on March 17, 2008.
decision: Begin regular production of Tesla Roadster.
actual_change: Tesla commenced regular production of the 2008 Roadster.
before_state: Tesla had a Roadster prototype and reservations.
after_state: Tesla had begun regular production of a production electric vehicle.
trigger: Validated demand and completed regulatory approvals.
outcome: Tesla converted Roadster concept into production vehicle.

evidence_text: Amazon states it went public on May 15, 1997.
decision: Complete initial public offering.
actual_change: Amazon went public at an IPO price of $18.00.
before_state: Amazon operated as a private online retailer.
after_state: Amazon had public-market financing and listed common stock.
trigger: Need capital to support growth of online retail operations.
outcome: Amazon completed its initial public offering.

evidence_text: Ford records first Model T shipment to a customer on October 1, 1908.
decision: Ship first Model T to customer.
actual_change: Ford shipped Model T to its first customer.
before_state: Ford sold earlier automobile models.
after_state: Ford had launched a durable, affordable Model T to customers.
trigger: Goal to create affordable, simple, durable vehicle.
outcome: Model T became Ford’s mass-market automobile.

source_title: Mickey Mouse to Celebrate His Birthday with a Trip Around the World
evidence_text: Disney records Steamboat Willie’s theatrical release at Colony Theatre on November 18, 1928.
decision: Release Steamboat Willie theatrically.
actual_change: Disney released Steamboat Willie, Mickey’s first theatrical film.
before_state: Disney studio produced animated films before Mickey’s first theatrical release.
after_state: Mickey’s sound-animation film reached theatrical audiences.
trigger: Need to differentiate animated entertainment with synchronized sound.
outcome: Mickey became Disney’s enduring global ambassador.

evidence_text: Pfizer records that 240,000 shares of new common stock were offered to public on June 22, 1942.
decision: Offer new common stock to public.
actual_change: Pfizer offered 240,000 shares of new common stock publicly.
before_state: Pfizer was privately held.
after_state: Pfizer had public shareholders.
trigger: Need capital for pharmaceutical growth.
outcome: Pfizer became publicly held.

evidence_text: Pfizer records FDA approval of Terramycin on March 15, 1950.
decision: Launch Terramycin under Pfizer label after FDA approval.
actual_change: Pfizer introduced Terramycin as its first pharmaceutical sold in United States under Pfizer label.
before_state: Pfizer had manufacturing and fermentation capabilities.
after_state: Pfizer had first proprietary branded pharmaceutical product and sales force.
trigger: FDA approval of Terramycin.
outcome: Terramycin established Pfizer-branded pharmaceutical selling.

evidence_text: Walmart records offering 300,000 common shares to public on October 1, 1970.
decision: Offer common shares to public.
actual_change: Walmart offered 300,000 shares at $16.50 per share.
before_state: Walmart was privately financed discount retailer.
after_state: Walmart had public shareholders and growth capital.
trigger: Need capital to expand discount-store network.
outcome: Walmart became publicly traded.

source_title: Visa Inc. Prices Initial Public Offering
evidence_text: Visa records its shares beginning NYSE trading on March 19, 2008 after initial public offering.
decision: List Visa shares on New York Stock Exchange.
actual_change: Visa shares began NYSE trading under ticker V.
before_state: Visa had completed global reorganization.
after_state: Visa operated as publicly traded company.
trigger: Global reorganization and public capital strategy.
outcome: Visa became public company.

evidence_text: Apple records initial public offering on December 12, 1980.
decision: Complete Apple initial public offering.
actual_change: Apple went public at $22 per share.
before_state: Apple was private personal-computer company.
after_state: Apple had public shareholders and growth capital.
trigger: Need capital to expand personal-computer business.
outcome: Apple completed initial public offering.

evidence_text: Microsoft records initial public offering on March 13, 1986.
decision: Complete Microsoft initial public offering.
actual_change: Microsoft went public at $21 per share.
before_state: Microsoft was private software company.
after_state: Microsoft had public shareholders and growth capital.
trigger: Need capital to expand software business.
outcome: Microsoft completed initial public offering.

evidence_text: American Tower records Class A common stock commenced NYSE trading on June 5, 1998 after separation from American Radio.
decision: Begin NYSE trading as independent American Tower.
actual_change: American Tower Class A stock commenced NYSE trading after separation from American Radio.
before_state: American Tower operated as part of American Radio Systems.
after_state: American Tower operated as independent publicly traded company.
trigger: Corporate separation after parent merger.
outcome: American Tower became independent public communications-infrastructure company.

source_title: FCX Completes Acquisition of Phelps Dodge
evidence_text: Freeport-McMoRan completed acquisition of Phelps Dodge on March 19, 2007.
decision: Acquire Phelps Dodge.
actual_change: FCX completed acquisition of Phelps Dodge.
before_state: Freeport-McMoRan operated as smaller mining company.
after_state: FCX became world’s largest publicly traded copper company.
trigger: Need diversified copper assets and global growth.
outcome: FCX transformed into major global copper producer.

evidence_text: AMB Property Corporation and ProLogis completed merger and became Prologis, Inc. on June 3, 2011.
decision: Merge AMB Property Corporation and ProLogis.
actual_change: AMB and ProLogis merged and became Prologis, Inc.
before_state: AMB and ProLogis operated as separate industrial REITs.
after_state: Combined Prologis operated as merged logistics real-estate company.
trigger: Need combined global logistics portfolio and scale.
outcome: Prologis became combined company.

evidence_text: Newmont completed acquisition of Newcrest Mining Limited on November 6, 2023.
decision: Acquire Newcrest Mining Limited.
actual_change: Newmont completed Newcrest acquisition.
before_state: Newmont operated without Newcrest portfolio.
after_state: Newmont combined Newcrest assets into its operating model.
trigger: Build leading gold business with copper production.
outcome: Newmont created world-leading gold company.

source_title: JPMorgan Chase and Bank One Joint Proxy Statement
evidence_text: J.P. Morgan & Co. merged into Chase Manhattan Corporation on December 31, 2000, which became J.P. Morgan Chase & Co.
decision: Merge J.P. Morgan & Co. into Chase Manhattan.
actual_change: Chase Manhattan changed name to J.P. Morgan Chase & Co. after merger.
before_state: Chase Manhattan and J.P. Morgan operated as separate financial institutions.
after_state: Combined JPMorgan Chase operated as diversified financial-services company.
trigger: Strategic combination of banking and investment franchises.
outcome: JPMorgan Chase corporate identity was formed.

evidence_text: Caterpillar completed acquisition of Bucyrus on July 8, 2011.
decision: Acquire Bucyrus International.
actual_change: Caterpillar completed acquisition of Bucyrus.
before_state: Caterpillar had mining equipment portfolio without Bucyrus.
after_state: Caterpillar integrated Bucyrus mining equipment business.
trigger: Expand mining leadership and product range.
outcome: Caterpillar created broader mining equipment group.

source_title: NextEra Energy completes acquisition of Gulf Power
evidence_text: NextEra Energy completed acquisition of Gulf Power on January 1, 2019.
decision: Acquire Gulf Power from Southern Company.
actual_change: NextEra completed acquisition of Gulf Power.
before_state: Gulf Power was part of Southern Company.
after_state: Gulf Power joined NextEra Energy family.
trigger: Expand utility customer base and energy portfolio.
outcome: NextEra added Gulf Power operations.

evidence_text: UnitedHealth Group subsidiary Optum completed DaVita Medical Group acquisition on June 19, 2019.
decision: Acquire DaVita Medical Group through Optum.
actual_change: Optum completed purchase of DaVita Medical Group.
before_state: UnitedHealth operated Optum without DaVita Medical Group.
after_state: Optum included acquired physician-care division.
trigger: Expand value-based care delivery capabilities.
outcome: UnitedHealth expanded care-delivery platform.

source_title: Caterpillar Kicks Off its Next 100 Years of Innovation and Industry Leadership
evidence_text: Caterpillar’s official centennial release says the company officially turns 100 on April 15, 2025, establishing April 15, 1925 as its formation date; it identifies the formation as the Holt Manufacturing Company and C. L. Best Tractor Co. merger.
decision: Merge Holt Manufacturing Company and C. L. Best Tractor Co. into Caterpillar Tractor Co.
actual_change: Caterpillar Tractor Co. formed through the Holt and C. L. Best merger.
before_state: Holt Manufacturing Company and C. L. Best Tractor Co. operated as separate equipment companies.
after_state: Caterpillar Tractor Co. began operating as combined company.
trigger: Both predecessor companies needed combined resources and technology after World War I.
outcome: Caterpillar began its first century as a combined industrial-equipment company.

evidence_text: Amazon’s 1997 SEC S-1 financial statements identify July 5, 1994 as company inception; same filing states Amazon was founded in July 1994.
decision: Form Amazon.com to build an online bookstore.
actual_change: Amazon.com began as an online bookstore on July 5, 1994.
before_state: No operating Amazon.com business existed.
after_state: Amazon.com began its company lifecycle as an online bookstore.
trigger: Opportunity to serve book customers through online commerce.
outcome: Amazon.com entered early development before website book sales began in July 1995.

source_title: Apple to celebrate 50 years of thinking different
evidence_text: Apple states that it was founded on April 1, 1976.
decision: Form Apple to develop personal computers.
actual_change: Apple formed on April 1, 1976.
before_state: Apple had not yet begun company operations.
after_state: Apple began operating as a personal-computer company.
trigger: Opportunity to bring personal computing to a broader audience.
outcome: Apple established its company lifecycle before Apple II launch.

source_title: Netflix.com Transforms DVD Business Eliminating Late Fees and Due Dates
evidence_text: Netflix announced its Marquee subscription program on December 16, 1999, replacing due dates and late fees with four DVDs per month for a set fee.
decision: Replace per-rental due dates and late fees with a subscription program.
actual_change: Netflix launched Marquee, a monthly subscription with four DVD rentals and no due dates or late fees.
before_state: Netflix offered DVD rentals and purchases online.
after_state: Netflix offered a repeatable subscription rental workflow.
trigger: Customer frustration with due dates and late fees.
outcome: Netflix established an early subscription-rental model.

source_title: Tesla Motors Begins Regular Production of 2008 Tesla Roadster
evidence_text: Tesla's investor-relations release states that its Roadster prototype was first unveiled on July 19, 2006.
decision: Publicly unveil a high-performance electric Roadster prototype.
actual_change: Tesla unveiled its Roadster prototype.
before_state: Tesla was developing an electric sports car.
after_state: Tesla had publicly demonstrated its first vehicle concept.
trigger: Need to validate demand for a high-performance electric vehicle.
outcome: The prototype generated early Roadster reservations.

source_title: American Tower historical public offering disclosure
evidence_text: American Tower's filing states that it completed a public offering of 27,861,987 Class A shares on July 8, 1998.
decision: Raise public equity capital after separation into a publicly traded tower company.
actual_change: American Tower completed a public offering of 27,861,987 Class A shares at $23.50 per share.
before_state: American Tower had separated into a publicly traded tower company.
after_state: American Tower had raised public equity to fund growth and obligations.
trigger: Capital needs after corporate separation and tower expansion.
outcome: American Tower strengthened capital for independent operations.

source_title: Prologis October 2013 prospectus: initial public offering date
evidence_text: Prologis' October 2013 prospectus dates its initial public offering to November 26, 1997. Its co-founder separately identifies the 1983 inception of AMB and consolidation of existing fund portfolios for the IPO.
decision: Take the established AMB real estate business public.
actual_change: AMB completed its initial public offering on November 26, 1997.
before_state: AMB had operated since 1983 with privately funded real estate portfolios.
after_state: The established real estate business operated through a publicly traded vehicle.
trigger: Consolidation of existing fund portfolios into a public investment vehicle.
outcome: Completion of the IPO; no claim of initial customer validation.

evidence_text: Visa's SEC filing states that from October 1 through October 3, 2007, Visa Inc. consummated restructuring that made Visa U.S.A., Visa International, Visa Canada and Inovant direct or indirect subsidiaries.
decision: Consolidate regional Visa entities under Visa Inc.
actual_change: Visa consummated global restructuring that made Visa U.S.A., Visa International, Visa Canada and Inovant subsidiaries of Visa Inc.
before_state: Visa regional entities operated through separate membership structures.
after_state: Visa operated through a global corporate holding structure.
trigger: Need to align global operations and prepare public-company structure.
outcome: Visa Inc. became global parent before its 2008 IPO.

source_title: 30 years a giant, UHG marches on
evidence_text: Healthcare Finance News reports that UnitedHealth Group became publicly traded on Friday, October 17, 1984.
decision: Become a publicly traded managed-health company.
actual_change: UnitedHealth Group became publicly traded.
before_state: United HealthCare operated as a private managed-health organization.
after_state: UnitedHealth Group had public-market capital and ownership.
trigger: Need capital and operating scale for health-plan growth.
outcome: Public listing enabled broader health-services expansion.

decision: Launch BankAmericard in Fresno through an initial cardholder and merchant network.
trigger: Need to validate a multi-merchant revolving-credit program in one city before wider expansion.
before_state: Bank of America had no launched consumer revolving-credit card network.
actual_change: Bank of America launched BankAmericard in Fresno and distributed cards to initial local cardholders after recruiting participating merchants.
after_state: BankAmericard operated as an initial multi-sided payments network in Fresno.
outcome: The launch established payment-network model that became Visa.
source_title: Roots of the Valley: Bank of America Launches New Credit Card in Fresno
evidence_text: Fresno City & County Historical Society records Bank of America launched its first credit card in Fresno on September 18, 1958; BankAmericard later became Visa.
